## Motivation
SGLang HiCache stores one logical page as several per-pool Mooncake objects, keyed as `{key_prefix}_{page_hash}{suffix}`. An external KV-aware router that wants to score L3 hits has to rebuild these keys, but the suffix depends on the model's pool layout, the parallelism layout, and the resolved `--page-size`, so deriving it outside the engine is fragile. Mooncake already models per-pool hit policies internally (`PoolHitPolicy`: ALL_PAGES / TRAILING_PAGES); this PR exposes the same information to external consumers.

This is the engine-side producer for the Dynamo KV router change (ai-dynamo/dynamo#14720), which uses this layout to reconstruct the object keys.

## Modifications

- New endpoint `GET /get_hicache_l3_cache_layout`, following the existing `GetInternalStateReq` tokenizer→scheduler round-trip. The same layout is also included as `hicache_object_layout` in HTTP `/server_info` and gRPC `GetServerInfo.json_info`.
- The layout lists the physical pools used by storage prefetch (primary KV, component pools such as SWA, and sidecar pools; logical anchors with no stored object are excluded). Each pool reports its key `suffixes`, `hit_policy` and `trailing_pages`. The layout also reports `key_prefix`, `is_mla_backend`, `pp_size` and `pp_rank`.
- Returns `"enabled": false` with a `reason` when hierarchical caching is disabled, the L3 backend is not Mooncake, the pools cannot be described (e.g. MHA or rank-sharded auxiliary pools, missing window metadata), or the scheduler replies are inconsistent.
- The layout is built by `MooncakeStore.describe_l3_object_layout`, which uses `_get_hybrid_page_component_keys`, the same key-building code the store writes objects with.
- The DP and Ray startup paths keep each scheduler's layout and return a merged result instead of the first reply; if replicas disagree, the layout is reported as unavailable. The merge helpers are in `hicache_storage.py`.
- CPU-only unit tests in `test/registered/hicache/test_hicache_l3_object_layout.py` (registered under `base-a-test-cpu`) with additional cases in `test_grpc_bridge.py`, `test_server_info.py` and `test_data_parallel_controller.py`, and a section in `docs/docs/advanced_features/hicache_design.mdx`.

Two scoping decisions, happy to revisit:
- The endpoint mirrors `/model_info` (no auth); can add `AuthLevel.ADMIN_OPTIONAL` to match the adjacent `/hicache/storage-backend` if preferred.
- With pipeline parallelism each stage stores objects under its own `pp_rank` suffix, so the merged layout lists the pools of every stage and reports `pp_rank: null`. If the layout cannot cover all `pp_size` stages (for example multi-node PP), it is reported as unavailable.

## Accuracy Tests
N/A — introspection-only change; does not affect model outputs.

Testing: the CPU unit tests above were run locally. GPU end-to-end runs on DeepSeek V4 with the Dynamo consumer were done on an earlier revision, before the latest merge from main, and have not been repeated on the current head.

## Speed Tests and Profiling
N/A — the endpoint is queried out-of-band by an external router and touches no inference path.

@@ -176,6 +176,14 @@ When a backend is attached, HiCache hands it the host memory pools in a fixed or
 
 Specifically, **LMCache**, an efficient KV cache layer for enterprise-scale LLM inference, provides an alternative solution to HiCache. Try LMCache [here](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/tree/main/python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/storage/lmcache).
 
+### External KV Router Integration
+
+HiCache is not only consumed inside SGLang. An external KV-aware router placed in front of the engines can also query the same L3 data to route requests to the instance that can reuse the most KV cache. Such a router must rebuild the exact object keys the backend uses, which for Mooncake is `{key_prefix}_{page_hash}{suffix}`. The suffix depends on the model's pool layout, the parallelism layout, and the resolved `--page-size`, so the engine exposes its layout instead of letting each router derive the naming itself.
+
+The Mooncake backend describes the physical KV primary, SWA/Mamba components, and registered sidecars; it excludes logical KV anchors with no buffer. Suffixes come from the write-path key builders. KV uses `all_pages`; SWA uses `trailing_pages` with its component's `full_window_pages`, and Mamba uses one trailing page. Sidecars retain their own hit policy and derive a trailing window from their index-source component.
+
+The startup handshake and `GET /get_hicache_l3_cache_layout` use the same layout generator. In `/server_info`, the outer `hicache_object_layout` field contains `{enabled, backend, page_size, hicache_object_layout: {pools, key_prefix, is_mla_backend, pp_rank, pp_size}}`; pool entries contain `pool`, `suffixes`, `hit_policy`, and optionally `trailing_pages`. External lookup is enabled only for rank-replicated/MLA pools, including DeepSeek V4 compressed MLA. With pipeline parallelism each stage stores objects under its own `pp_rank` suffix, so the layout lists the pools of every stage and reports `pp_rank: null`; a layout that cannot cover all `pp_size` stages (for example when some stages run on other nodes) is unavailable. MHA or rank-sharded auxiliary pools, missing window metadata, unavailable Mooncake, and inconsistent scheduler replies also return `enabled: false` with a `reason`. Consumers must not register L3 in that case; an absent outer field indicates an older engine and permits legacy fallback. Ordinary DP and Ray startup retain and check scheduler replies rather than selecting the first layout.
+
 ## Related Parameters
 
 - **`--enable-hierarchical-cache`**: Enable hierarchical cache functionality. This is required to use HiCache.
